defect_origin: fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 (Federico Ficarelli 2022-08-25, [LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms) added PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp; later fork commits 8f9832300f0e/bded3e51fd64 do not touch the defective logic
root_cause: Block placement runs after PULPHardwareLoops. PULPFixupHwLoops (f1b7aebff8c2) (1) used MachineLoop::getBottomBlock(), which derefs MF.end() when the loop ends the function (reported k05 -O3 crash); (2) when the latch was not the last loop block after the header (rotated above the header, or loop blocks placed after it) retargeted the loop end to the bottom block, leaving the latch outside the range (k05 -O2 1.7x work; seed 270 wrong result); (3) did not handle loops with several back edges (tail-duplicated latch): iterations via the copy are uncounted (seed 61 wrong; seeds 22/13 hang with attempt 1); (4) used L->getExitBlock() as the fall-out target, null with early exits or repeated exit edges -> exit branch erased with no replacement; (5) past-the-end reads: getDebugLoc before end() check, bump rule counting branches, and an empty latch (compare-only latch) in fixupLoopInstrs (notes/20/F005-reduced-emptylatch.ll also crashes int-20).
fix: removeUncountableLoops (first): delete the LOOPsetup (keep software loop, whose branches are still intact) when L->getLoopLatch()==null (several back edges) or the latch has !=1 out-of-loop successor - justified bail-out, hardware has one counting and one fall-out point. fixupLoopLayout: move rotated latch (+contiguous loop blocks before it) after the bottom, or the unique latch alone to the end when other loop blocks follow it; fallthrough repair as ARMBlockPlacement::moveBasicBlock (ARMBlockPlacement.cpp:246 @llvmorg-20.1.8); old 'update end to bottom' kept only when the setup block is not the latch. fixupLoopLatch: ExitBlock = latch's own exit (getLatchExit) instead of L->getExitBlock(), so 'Bcc exit; j header' is replaced by 'j exit' in the same round. getLayoutBottom replaces getBottomBlock. getDebugLoc inside the end() check. Bump rule: latch counts non-terminators (<=1 keeps), other blocks keep old size()<=2. NOP inserted when the latch has no instruction to label (same as existing inline-asm workaround).
not_in_PULPHardwareLoops: Root cause is entirely in PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp; PULPHardwareLoops.cpp (F003) untouched.
